Scotland’s ramped-up second-half performance offered some cause for optimism as Sébastien Pocognoli’s tenure as head coach began with a goalless draw with Slovenia in Ljubljana.

The 39-year-old Belgian head coach, appointed in August as Steve Clarke’s successor, refreshed the side for the Nations League Group B1 opener in the Stozice Stadium, but they were fortunate on a couple of occasions at least not to fall behind before rallying before the break.

Scotland had been insipid and uninspiring for most of the first half but after the interval they played with pace and purpose as Slovenia captain and goalkeeper Jan Oblak became a key figure, making saves from Oli McBurnie and Kieron Bowie.

Oli McBurnie spurns a chance for Scotland.It remains goalless between Slovenia and Scotland.📺 Watch on BBC One pic.twitter.com/sldzhNCGGb.

“It took us a bit of getting used to in the first half, the way the gaffer wants to play,” McBurnie told BBC Scotland.

“We created enough chances to win the game. I should have scored. I was asked to play a different position and I enjoyed it. I’d rather be getting in the positions than not getting chances.

In a recent development, “Second half was a lot more of what the manager wanted from us. It was waves of pressure and the only thing missing was a goal or two.”.

However, the goal that would have made the former Union Saint-Gilloise and Monaco manager’s debut as an international boss more memorable ultimately failed to arrive.

In this extended international break, the Scots will host Switzerland at Hampden on Tuesday and then travel to North Macedonia before taking on Slovenia in Glasgow, with the Tartan Army hoping to see further improvement – and goals.

September 29: Scotland vs Switzerland.

October 3: North Macedonia vs Scotland.

October 6: Scotland vs Slovenia.

November 13: Scotland vs North Macedonia.

November 16: Switzerland vs Scotland.

Speaking to BBC Scotland, the debutant remarked: “Thought we struggled to get into the game first half, but second half we completely dominated the game.

“They’ve got a top goalie who made really good saves. So many positives to take and a clean sheet as well.

“We changed shape a wee bit at half-time to get more control and that did really well for us.

“It’s a big game again on Tuesday so it’s important to recover now and go again.

“I’ve played on the left-hand side for a couple of years now, so I’m comfortable doing that.

“We’ve had a great week. A newly introduced manager, new way of playing and new faces in camp. It’s just the chances we need to take - the fact we’re creating the chances stands us in good stead.”.

The striker told BBC Scotland: “It took us a bit of getting used to in the first half, the way the gaffer wants to play.

Industry observers note that “We created enough chances to win the game. I should have scored.

In a recent development, “I was asked to play a different position and I enjoyed it. I’d rather be getting in the positions than not getting chances.

“Second half was a lot more of what the manager wanted from us. It was waves of pressure and the only thing missing was a goal or two.”.

Pocognoli’s first game in charge of Scotland ends in a goalless draw. The visitors produced a dominant second-half display, but their final ball and end-product was severely lacking in crucial moments. Ure, Hickey, Gilmour, McBurnie and Bowie all came close to scoring, but no one could break the deadlock.

Scotland cannot find a way past the impenetrable Oblak. There will be just two minutes of added time for the visitors to possibly score a late winner.

Lovric clatters into Gilmour and is cautioned. Slovenia can’t get out. It’s wave after wave of Scottish pressure.

Industry observers note that oblak comes out and fails to claim Robertson’s free-kick. The ball is recycled and the Tottenham full-back whips a second cross into the box and Slovenia fail to clear. Welsh is waiting for it, but lashes a first-time volley over the bar.

Karnicnik catches Robertson with a late lunging tackle and receives a yellow card, giving Scotland a chance to get the ball into the box.

The hosts make their fifth alteration of the afternoon, with Cerin withdrawn and Lovric on instead.

How has Bowie missed?! Gilmour finds Bowie with an outstanding pass through the centre of Slovenia’s defence. The substitute takes a touch then scuffs a rushed finish wide. Bowie has to do better there!

Another change is here for Scotland, with Gannon-Doak on to replace Hickey.

Another big chance for Scotland. This time Sassuolo's Kieron Bowie goes close.Slovenia 0-0 Scotland - watch the closing stages on BBC One. pic.twitter.com/xMe5gRNgEr.

From the resulting corner, Oblak is there again to thwart McBurnie’s point-blank header. The referee then blows his whistle to relieve the pressure on Slovenia. Somehow, the scoreline remains goalless.

The hosts make another double change as Sporar and Brekalo depart for Vipotnik and Balkovec.

Welsh spots Bowie’s run and threads a perfectly-weighted pass through to the forward. From an unfavourable angle, the substitute’s one-on-one attempt is blocked by Oblak.

Another massive chance for Scotland! McGinn’s searching corner is met by Hickey, who flicks a header wide of the far post. Scotland’s second-half performance deserves a goal.

Pocognoli orders Scotland’s first alteration of the game, with Bowie replacing Ure up top.

Hickey finds himself very high up the pitch and tries to tee up Ure with a cushioned header, but there isn’t enough power on the pass.

Gilmour and Ure link up effectively on the counter, but the latter’s pull-back is intercepted by Drkusic.

Slovenia then make two changes as Zabukovnik and Zec replace Elsnik and Drkusic.

McGinn strides forward and tries to find Ure, but Slovenia rush back to scramble it clear. Scotland are really pushing for the opening goal.

Recent findings suggest that gilmour and McBurnie play a devastating one-two, allowing the midfielder to advance into the penalty area. He shoots and aims for the far corner, but his placed effort is collected impressively by Oblak, who makes another crucial intervention.

The second half has started as the first ended, with Scotland applying all of the pressure. Slovenia have Oblak to thank for the goalless scoreline.

Sources indicate that mcBurnie and Oblak both challenge for the ball, with the Scotsman bumping into the goalkeeper, giving Slovenia a goal kick. The decision is met by a chorus of boos from the away fans.

It has been revealed that mcBurnie latches onto a loose ball and skips away from Drkusic’s sliding challenge. One-on-one, the striker tries to round Oblak, but the Slovenian goalkeeper does sensationally to apprehend him. Upon reflection, it looks like McBurnie should have just shot and tried to put the ball between Oblak’s legs. He did the hard part, but lacked a clinical finish.

Oli McBurnie spurns a chance for Scotland.It remains goalless between Slovenia and Scotland.📺 Watch on BBC One pic.twitter.com/sldzhNCGGb.

Sources indicate that mcGinn brilliantly turns Drkusic on the halfway line and then tees up Gilmour. The Napoli midfielder tries to float a pass over to the onrushing Robertson, but he hits the switch of play straight out for a throw-in. In defence of Gilmour, the pitch really doesn’t look in the best condition, with various players struggling regarding their weight of pass.

We are back under way for the second half. Both sides are unchanged at the break.

Pocognoli’s Scotland finished the half as the better side, but an opening goal has proved to be elusive. At times, they’ve looked suspect defensively and have lacked rhythm going forward. However, Pocognoli’s squad have only been together for a few days and are playing in a new system. Can they produce a more inspired second-half performance?

Sources indicate that despite Scotland’s late push for an opening goal at the end of the first half, the two sides head in level at the break. Slovenia started on the front-foot, with Sporar and Drkusic both going close for the hosts, before Ure struck the post to be denied a dream debut goal.

HALF TIME: Slovenia 0-0 Scotland.No goals at the break in Ljubljana.#SVNSCO pic.twitter.com/6VGFRprBiz.

Ure strikes the woodwork! The Sevilla striker is agonisingly close to a debut goal for his country. He cuts inside to work some space and fires a low effort at goal, but his shot hits the post.

Scotland's best chance of the game so far 😯 Sevilla striker and debutant Robbie Ure strikes the post just before half-time.However, it remains goalless at the break.📺 Watch Slovenia v Scotland on BBC One 🇸🇮 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 pic.twitter.com/fm1wH2fOej.

Recent findings suggest that much better from Scotland! McGinn turns his marker and clips a wonderful pass over to Ure, who has drifted out wide. The ball is then delivered into the box toward McGinn, whose header bounces off McBurnie. Hickey is arriving to pounce on the loose ball, but the wing-back’s effort is blocked by the Slovenian defence.

According to recent reports, robertson picks up the game’s first yellow card for an off-the-ball incident. The Scotland captain is clearly very unhappy with the decision as we await to see a replay. Nevertheless, the action resumes with a Slovenia free-kick.

Sources indicate that slovenia go close again as a corner is whipped in. Drkusic wins the header at the near post and it bounces off the outside of the near post. That is definitely another warning sign for Scotland.

Industry observers note that matko goes on the outside of Welsh, and from a tight angle, he shoots, but his fizzed effort saves the side netting of the near post. Some fans behind the goal cheer because they think it’s gone in, but their view has really deceived them.

Sources indicate that it’s been a quiet afternoon for both goalkeepers so far, with neither yet to make a noteworthy save. On a couple of occasions, Slovenia have had encouraging opportunities to get the ball into the Scotland’s box, but the deliveries have been overhit and poorly executed.

In a recent development, similarly to Scotland, Slovenia are also playing a tremendously high-line. Unlike Slovenia, Scotland have been unable to find the right pass in behind the home side’s defence. Gilmour then carelessly gives the ball away as Scotland’s latest spell of possession ends.

Since Slovenia wasted that 14th-minute chance, Scotland have grown into the contest and are beginning to look comfortable in possession. However, they’re still waiting to craft their first notable opening here.

The hosts miss a huge chance! Once again, Sturm gets in behind Scotland’s incredibly high line and then fires a low cross into the penalty area. Sporar then beats McKenna to the delivery, but taps his close-range effort wide of the far post from inside the six-yard box. That’s a massive let-off for Scotland...

According to recent reports, matko is unleashed by a drilled pass then pierces through a gap between Robertson and Welsh. The Slovenia winger drives into the penalty area and tries to find either Sturm or Sporar with a cross, but Hendry does magnificently to make a last-ditch clearance.

It has been revealed that slovenia have the ball in the net, but the offside flag is up. Sturm gets in behind Scotland’s defence and slides a low cross into Sporar’s path. The striker then sweeps a composed first-time effort into the top corner. It’s a brilliant finish, but Sturm was miles offside in the build-up.

Sources indicate that gunn comes out confidently to collect a looping cross, before the ball is launched forward in McBurnie’s direction. The Hull City striker and Ure are playing really close to each other, very much like an old-school front-two.

Slovenia forward Sturm is wiped out by Hendry’s wild early challenge. The Scotland defender is perhaps lucky to avoid a booking. Welsh then heads the resulting set-piece away and out for a corner.

The hosts get us underway in the Slovenian capital. Can Pocognoli begin his Scotland tenure with a Nations League victory?

Both teams are out on the pitch in Ljubljana. We are moments away from the start of the Pocognoli era.

New Scotland manager Sebastien Pocognoli sings Flower of Scotland as he takes charge of the national side for the first time 🎶 🇸🇮 Slovenia v Scotland 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 is live on BBC One now.#BBCFootball #NationsLeague pic.twitter.com/I2aeqYkNGB.

On paper, it looks like Sebastien Pocognoli has opted for a five-back formation, with Swansea City defender Stephen Welsh making his Scotland debut as one of the centre backs.

Captain Andy Robertson and Brentford’s Aaron Hickey will operate as the wing-backs, with Billy Gilmour, Lewis Ferguson and John McGinn forming a midfield three.

A newly introduced-look attack is spearheaded by the returning Oli McBurnie and 22-year-old Robbie Ure, who like Welsh, will also make his Scotland debut.

Angus Gunn remains his country’s first-choice goalkeeper.

Recent findings suggest that debutants Robbie Ure and Stephen Welsh are each poised for their first international cap. Billy Gilmour returns to the starting XI after missing the World Cup through injury and Oli McBurnie will make his first appearance for Scotland since 2021.

Sébastien Pocognoli's first Scotland starting XI 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿#SVNSCO pic.twitter.com/JC6RGOq1QJ.

“The first game is always a special game so you have to bring the mental aspect in for the players and for the staff.

Industry observers note that “A good result can help but the most vital thing is we see things that we work on through the week. I hope is we apply that well then we will get the result which will be the perfect mix.

It has been revealed that “I hope we can bring a good game, and a good exciting principle on the pitch. I think we need the support from the supporters because there’s a lot of new players.

“We need to create a good energy but it’s up to us on the pitch to create this. So then we can be hand in hand with the supporters.”.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this UEFA Nations League B, Group 1 match as Slovenia host Scotland at Stozice Stadium in Ljubljana.

Recent findings suggest that scotland qualified for their first World Cup in 28 years this summer, but they exited the tournament with a whimper after failing to finish as one of the best third-place group sides. Steve Clarke’s men beat tournament debutants Haiti 1-0 in their opening match, before falling to defeats without scoring against Morocco and Brazil.

Recent findings suggest that following the World Cup, Clarke stepped down as Scotland’s head coach, ending a seven-year tenure, and was replaced by Belgian manager Sebastien Pocognoli. The former Monaco boss will take charge of his first game in his new role today and will be itching to make an encouraging start in a new era for Scottish football.

Over this extended international break, Pocognoli’s side will also face Switzerland and North Macedonia, as well as a return fixture against Slovenia in Scotland on October 6 to round off a busy period.

While Scotland took part in the World Cup, Slovenia were reflecting on their hugely disappointing qualification performance, where they finished third in their group behind Switzerland and Kosovo without winning and netting just three goals across six matches.

Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko – Slovenia’s star man and most well-known player – withdrew from Bostjan Cesar’s squad earlier this week after the recurrence of a shin injury caused the 23-year-old to completely miss the 1-1 draw against Fulham last Sunday.

Scotland have a few notable absences, with Scott McTominay, Che Adams and Lawrence Shankland all unavailable, but Billy Gilmour returns to the fold after missing the World Cup through injury, Oli McBurnie has been recalled and Sevilla striker Robbie Ure has received his first senior call-up.

Kick-off is at 14:00, with team news coming shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The win came in Kevin Blackwell’s first game as permanent manager after his appointment earlier this week.

A goal in either half from Kai Jennings, Pemi Aderoju and a resolute back-line performance earned Crawley a deserved win.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

It takes the Reds to within three points from safety, with as many games in hand against 22nd-placed Rochdale.

Reds made a fast start to the first half and took the lead in the fourth minute through Jennings, following Kellan Gordon’s cross from a darting run down the right wing.

Fleetwood, Arsenal’s conquerors and League Cup quarter-finalists, failed to clear their lines on the edge of the six-yard box and Jennings pounced on their indecision to smash home into the roof of the net.

New Reds centre back Ben Heneghan blocked a well-hit shot from range in the Cod Army’s first effort on goal in the ninth minute.

Vito Mannone calmy claimed Jake Batty’s left-wing cross to dispel Fleetwood as the away side got a foothold in the game and started to up the pressure, shortly before Reds nervily dealt with an Andy Cannon cross.

On the 15-minute mark Aderoju found himself through one-on-one but shot straight into the welcoming arms of Fleetwood keeper Jay Lynch.

Mannone was called upon to punch clear a couple of searching Fleetwood crosses into the box and lifted the pressure of his side in an open context.

Dylan Mogan nearly put the Reds 2-0 up on the half hour, he tricked his way past the Fleetwood right-back but curling shot from the edge of the box clipped the post and went out for a goal kick.

Just before the break Fleetwood’s Aaron Loupal-Bi got into a good position on the left after a one-two but his tame effort along the ground was collected by Mannone.

Reds flew out the traps to double their lead within a minute of the restart, Morgan stormed through Fleetwood’s midfield and slotted Aderoju in on-goal and the significant target man rifled a left-foot shot into the back of the net.

The visitors responded by almost pulling one back from a curling shot from the edge of the box and then hit the post moments afterwards.

Reds first chance of the second half fell to Aderoju who rose well but headed just wide from Gordon’s good right-side delivery.

Fleetwood gave themselves a lifeline thanks to substitute Will Davies’ firing a shot past Mannone from the middle of the penalty area to give the travelling fans behind the goal a reason to cheer.

Reds matched Fleetwood as the physicality grew as the half wore on and dug in to match their opponents.

Fleetwood substitute Lewis McCann stung the gloves of Mannone and produced a match-winning save from the big Italian who’s clean sheet was hard-earned.

Duke-McKenna had the chance to seal the points for the Reds at the end after chopping back onto his left foot down the right side, but his curled shot was parried away by Lynch.

Crawley are back at Broadfield in league action again this Tuesday (November 24) as they aim to climb out of the drop-zone in a tough test against high-flying Barnet.

Hearts travel to Dundee on Saturday evening as the Scottish Premiership swings back into action following the international break.

Wouter Vrancken’s injury-hit side are looking for a major turnaorund after collecting just one win from their last eight matches in all competitions, a run which included an Edinburgh derby defeat to Hibs in the Premier Sports Cup semi-final at Hampden.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The 5-2 hammering at the hands of Falkirk at Tynecastle before the break - Hearts were 5-0 down inside 47 minutes - also shattered their unbeaten home record stretching back 18 months.

Injuries have been a huge factor in Hearts’ downturn with a full starting team of players ruled out in recent weeks.

Hearts go into the match in fourth place in the table, three points ahead of fifth-placed Dundee, who have earned plaudits this season after collecting 17 points from their opening 12 matches.

Steven Pressley’s side have been particularly strong at home, where they are unbeaten in four matches, with the vast majority of their points accrued from their games at Dens Park this season.

It has been revealed that the Scottish Premiership match between Dundee and Hearts takes place at Dens Park, Dundee on Saturday, November 21, 2026. Kick-off is 5.45pm.

The match will be broadcast live on Premier Sports 1 with coverage starting at 5.15pm. Highlights will be shown on Sportscene on BBC One Scotland at 10.20pm.

Dundee are still without long-term absentees Bobby Wales (ankle), Simon Murray, Finlay Robertson and Jack Moorhouse (all ACL), but Steven Pressley expects everyone else to be available.

Hearts’ injury list has eased slightly, with Ageu, Christian Borchgrevink and Rogers Mato back in contention, but Malachi Fagan-Walcott (muscle) joins Stephen Kingsley (hamstring), Calvin Miller (knee), Tomas Magnusson (concussion), Harry Milne (knee), Oisin McEntee (muscle), Craig Halkett (Achilles), Blair Spittal (shin) and Tom Renaud (ankle) in being unavailable.

115 charges distraction? Enzo Maresca addresses Man City’s slump in form and “avoidable” problem

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (807 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Oliver Thomas | 20 Nov 2026 17:36.
  • Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has dismissed suggestions that the Premier League financial charges case is affecting his players following a concerning dip in form.
  • In September, an independent commission found Man City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the investigation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 20 Nov 2026 17:36.

Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has dismissed suggestions that the Premier League financial charges case is affecting his players following a concerning dip in form.

In September, an independent commission found Man City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the investigation.

The Citizens are accused of using "sham" contracts and bogus deals to disguise more than £830m in secret funding and artificially inflate revenues between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

Man City continue to plead their innocence, stating that “a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case,” and they have subsequently lodged an appeal.

A wide range of potential sanctions have been mooted for Man City should their guilty verdict be upheld, including heavy fines, transfer bans, stripping titles, points deductions leading to relegation and expulsion from the Premier League.

On the pitch, Man City responded to the bombshell news with a statement 3-0 Premier League win away against Liverpool, but they have since won just four of their last eight games in all competitions (including one in the EFL Cup on penalties).

Maresca’s side entered November’s international break after a disappointing run of three consecutive Premier League defeats to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest, losing 3-1 away to the latter a fortnight ago.

The Citizens have conceded 17 goals across their last nine matches and have failed to keep a clean sheet in that time, while some first-team stars have come under fire for making costly errors leading to goals.

Man City currently sit third in the Premier League table, six points behind leaders Arsenal who will welcome the Sky Blues to the Emirates Stadium next week.

Maresca’s players have regularly faced media questions over the ongoing financial charges case, and while the Man City boss accepts that those queries are fair game, he insists the concern is not affecting results on the pitch.

"If you ask, they need to answer and if you ask me I need to answer," Maresca told reporters at a press conference on Friday.

It has been revealed that "I'm here to answer, so if you are going to ask the players because they want to be polite they need to give you an answer. If you don't want to talk about that don't ask the players about the noise.

In a recent development, "I don't think the players are thinking too much about that. If we want to relate the noise with the defeat, Villa away we had so many chances - for instance, Iliman [Ndiaye] hit the post, Brighton's keeper was Man of the Match, at Forest where Erling [Haaland] had the chance to score [to make it] 2-2. I don't think the players are focused on the noise.".

This comes after former Manchester United defender Gary Neville suggested after City’s loss at Forest that Maresca’s players are being affected by the off-field scandal.

According to recent reports, speaking on NBC Sports, Neville mentioned: "It's all everybody's talking about back home in the last month or so and those players will be getting asked constantly: 'What do you think is going to happen? What happens if they do get relegated, will you stay?'.

“Imagine that your family is having to put up with that, your agent is continually thinking about those things so it can't be ruled out as a factor that that's going to start to seep in.

"Obviously if you lose a football match or two that's going to start to look like an excuse but they have to play better, compete in games, make sure that they do better from a tactical and physical perspective.

“But I do believe it will be having some impact just because of the weight of what's been hitting them from a publicity point of view in the last four to six weeks.".

Explaining what he believes is the main reason behind Man City’s recent decline, Maresca noted: "For sure, we are conceding avoidable goals. For instance, the third goal against Forest. They have 11 players inside the box defending and we concede the third goal.

“We reviewed things during the international break that we need to do better, and again, the idea is to continue to attack in the same way, creating chances, and trying to find the balance when we defend or when we are building like what happened with the first goal against Forest, where if we can avoid mistakes, it's always better.".

Maresca now faces an urgent tactical puzzle ahead of Saturday's clash with Fulham, as he bids to fix the glaring midfield imbalance and address the dilemma he has with Enzo Fernandez.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Celtic manager Martin O’Neill hopes Luke McCowan’s performance in the 4-1 win over St Mirren can be a catalyst to reignite his Parkhead career.

It has been revealed that O’Neill watched his side open up a seven-point gap on second-placed Rangers, who face Motherwell on Saturday evening, blowing away St Mirren before half-time thanks to goals from Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain (33), Camilo Duran (40) and McCowan (42). Callum McGregor (63) added a fourth, with Killian Phillips (69) scoring a consolation penalty for the away side.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Dealt a double blow ahead of the game, midfield pair Benjamin Nygren and Mika Baur both ruled out after picking up injuries on international duty, O’Neill handed McCowan his first start in over two months in the centre of the park alongside Oxlade-Chamberlain.

Industry observers note that mcCowan has suffered in the last few months, dropping out of the matchday squad after a high-profile error in the defeat to LASK during the Champions League playoffs. Forced to delete his Instagram account to escape personal abuse from sections of the online support, the former Dundee captain had played just 14 minutes since being hauled off at half-time in a 1-0 home defeat to Rangers on September 20.

In a recent development, “I thought he did really well for us,” was O’Neill’s assessment of McCowan’s return to the starting line-up. “It was his first full game for a considerable amount of time. He got the ball once and he played it almost blindly and it was intercepted and I thought ‘oh gosh, here we go’. But he roared back. Took the goal great, and I’m really pleased for him because he’s a really genuine lad.

“It has been tough [for him]. I thought in the game against Rangers, he was thrown into position, and it didn’t start well for him in the match. I thought it felt like deja vu for him after his last game against Rangers at the back end of last season, too. For him today, I felt that was a significant boost for him. I’m pleased that there’s a bit of competition for places [in midfield] now. Which is good. But I am pleased that him and Alex got on the field and were able to play. That itself is a confidence booster.”.

According to recent reports, duran had the ball in the net for Celtic after five minutes but assistant referee signalled for an offside. The home side thought they’d taken the lead again just after the quarter hour mark, with Duran the disappointed party once more. Blasting home the rebound after Jota’s shot was parried away by Jacob Chapman, the frustrated Colombian looked to sky as the flag went up for offside in the build up for a second time.

A misplaced pass from McCowan signalled a groan from the home crowd as Celtic frustration crept in, however, they needn’t have worried, finding their opener via Oxlade-Chamberlain just after the half-hour mark, with the experienced midfielder slamming home from close range after a positive forward run and cross from Hyun-Jun Yang on the right-wing.

It was no less than the home side deserved, but the momentary VAR check for the opener followed by a blocked goal-bound effort from Killian Phillips offered some unexpected anxiety in the immediate aftermath. O’Neill’s side added further unnecessary stress on a bitterly cold Glasgow afternoon when Yang somehow failed to square to Duran when clean through on goal.

The striker finally got on the scoresheet with a fine side-footed finish from a Kieran Tierney cross shortly before the break.

A moment of redemption followed just 120 seconds later when the returning McCowan collected a neat cut back from Jota in the area to fire home first time beyond Chapman, effectively killing the game before the break.

Industry observers note that his first goal since the 5-1 win over Kilmarnock on August 9, a relatively muted celebration followed from McCowan as he was congratulated by his teammates. Virtually out of the picture at Celtic in recent weeks, he’ll hope it’s not his last and that his unexpected reprieve can lead to an extended spell in his boyhood club’s engine room. The victory already wrapped up in nine first-half minutes, McGregor’s placed shot added to the scoreline just after the hour mark, with Phillips’ penalty after a foul from goalkeeper Sam Johnstone on Calvin Ramsay in the box just a consolation.

O’Neill also addressed the omission of Haissem Hassan during his press-match conference and the fitness of Baur and Alistair Johnston. Quashing rumours that the Egyptian was left out against Kilmarnock prior to the international break because he was “unpopular” within the squad earlier this week, the 74-year-old has insisted that both Hassan and Kasper Hogh, who was an unused substitute, will have a part to play against Torreense in the Europa League on Thursday night.

“Kasper will be ready for Thursday,” remarked O’Neill. “That’s the point. We’re going to need him on Thursday. For want of a better word, it’s more rotation than anything else. Kasper is fine. He’ll [Haissem] will be there for Thursday as well. He’s missed a couple of games. He didn’t come back until Friday from the international break, a couple of them didn’t.

“We were worried about Duran after he travelled halfway around the world, but he was amazing in training.

“Baur is in a boot. If that injury stretches to end of January, we’ll think about making a change [to the Europa League squad]. Alistair was getting a scan and some treatment this weekend in Dublin. We’ll find out about that and get an enhancement. I’m hoping it’s going to be good news. He’s feeling decent within himself now.”.

An inspiral of a star inside a common envelope with its giant companion

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 41 min read (8140 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~41 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The formation of compact stellar binaries requires rapid orbital tightening of their progenitor binary stars1,2.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The formation of compact stellar binaries requires rapid orbital tightening of their progenitor binary stars1,2. This is theorized to happen through common envelope evolution (CEE)3, when the stars orbit in a loosely bound, shared convective envelope, triggering an inspiral due to frictional drag4,5. However, this inspiral in such a system has never been observed directly. Here we present observations of AT 2025abao, a transient eruption in the Andromeda Galaxy, which originates from the CEE of an approximately 7M⊙ asymptotic giant branch (AGB) star with its companion. Extensive pre- and post-eruption spectroscopy is best explained as an approximately 0.7M⊙ companion inspiralling within the convective AGB envelope that powers a seven-year period of gradual brighteningone of the first direct observations of frictional drag energy dissipation induced by CEE. This phase is radiatively efficient, consistent with predictions for convective transport in CEE5,6,7,8. The subsequent merger of the companion with the primary core powers the ejection of the outermost 10% of the stellar envelope at speeds about 10× the primary escape speed, and empirically constrains the fraction of dissipated orbital energy available to unbind the convective common envelope4,9,10,11, 0.01 ≲ α ≲ 0.4. This end-to-end characterization using multi-survey observations demonstrates a path towards mapping the landscape of CEE outcomes with upcoming surveys.

All ground-based optical and near-IR photometry and spectra, together with the JWST and SPHEREx SEDs presented in this paper, are available for download from Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22948026). This repository also contains the bolometric parameters inferred from our SED fits. The JWST images are publicly available through the Mikulski Archive for Space Telescopes (https://doi.org/10.17909/07j6-dq13), and the SPHEREx Quick Release 2 (QR2) images are publicly available at IRSA.

The code used for the analysis of spectra and SEDs used in this paper is available on GitHub at https://github.com/virajkaram/at2025abao/. Any additional code or data can be obtained from the corresponding author upon request.

Optical spectra of the AT 2025abao eruption. Its spectral evolution matches the characteristic evolution seen in LRNe — blue continuum with emission lines at early times that transitions to a red continuum with molecular absorption features at late times.

It has been revealed that near-infrared spectra of AT 2025abao, from its precursor phase (red) and the eruption (blue). The spectra during the precursor phase resemble late M-type stars, while those during the eruption highlights a transition to hotter temperatures. Notably, the CO absorption bands are seen in all spectra, indicating that some molecular gas remains intact even after the eruption.

See section ‘Modelling the progenitor SED’ for details.

See section ‘SPHEREx pre-outburst SED modelling’ for details.

See section ‘Post-outburst JWST and SPHEREx SED modelling’ for details.

Theoretically calculated dust mass around the quiescent progenitor system as a function of binary mass ratio using analytical prescriptions (black line) and detailed simulations (squares). The black shaded region marks the range expected by varying stellar parameters in the analytical model (section ‘Comparisons to theoretical predictions of enhanced mass loss’). The observed dust mass from the archival progenitor SED and the JWST observation is shown in purple, which constrains the system mass ratio to \(q=0.1{0}_{-0.08}^{+0.10}\).

Industry observers note that previously identified sources such as V1309Sco, M31-LRN-2015, AT 2019zhd (circles) exhibit a gradual brightening by several magnitudes prior to its eruption. AT 2025abao (stars) differs from these sources, as it only highlights a bumpy  ≈ 1 magnitude brightening before transitioning to its eruption.

Evolution of FWHM velocities inferred from our spectra (red), compared to theoretical expectations for momentum-conserving collisions with CBM following a ρ(r) ∝ r−2 density profile (blue solid line). The broken lines indicate the expectation by including an additional mechanical power source, such as a surviving binary, injecting momentum into the ejecta. Our observations constrain the magnitude of this power source \(\mathop{E}\limits^{.}\lesssim 1{0}^{40}\) erg s−1.

LRNe for which progenitor primary stars have been identified are plotted as coloured points, colour-coded by the binding energy of the star. LRNe with no progenitor identifications are plotted as grey points. The eruption of AT 2025abao (star) is remarkably similar to other LRNe, despite having a progenitor with the lowest binding energy ever measured.

Sources indicate that a, The quiescent binary system comprising a  ≈ 7 M⊙ AGB and a  ≈ 0.7 M⊙ star, surrounded by an extended dust shell from mass loss from the binary following Roche Lobe overflow of the primary. b, The precursor brightening phase that began in 2018, marking the onset of CEE, powered by frictional drag on the inspiraling companion lasting for  ≈ 7 years. The mass outflow rate during this phase is  ~10−2 M⊙ yr−1, producing  ~0.1 M⊙ of CBM in an equatorial disk around the binary (dark brown). c, The ballistic eruption in late 2025 from the merger of the inspiraling companion with the primary core, resulting in the ejection of  ≈ 0.1 − 0.2 M⊙ of the primary envelope, and sublimation of a large fraction of dust around the binary. d, The eventual lightcurve powered by shock-interactions between freely expanding merger ejecta (indicated by yellow arrows) and equatorially focused CBM. The surviving pre-existing dust is traced by our JWST observations. The black arrows between the panels indicate the progression of time.

Serie A overtakes Premier League in stunning goalscoring turnaround – what has changed?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (969 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 20 Nov 2026 17:38.
  • Serie A has overtaken the Premier League as Europe's second-highest-scoring major domestic competition this season, completing a remarkable transformation from the lowest-scoring of the continent's top five leagues just a year ago.
  • After 110 matches in the 2026-27 campaign, Italy's top flight has produced 342 goals, an average of 3.11 per game, compared with the Premier League's 273 goals in 100 fixtures, or 2.73 per match.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 20 Nov 2026 17:38.

Serie A has overtaken the Premier League as Europe's second-highest-scoring major domestic competition this season, completing a remarkable transformation from the lowest-scoring of the continent's top five leagues just a year ago.

After 110 matches in the 2026-27 campaign, Italy's top flight has produced 342 goals, an average of 3.11 per game, compared with the Premier League's 273 goals in 100 fixtures, or 2.73 per match.

Only the Bundesliga, averaging 3.48 goals, currently ranks higher among Europe's five major leagues, with Ligue 1 and La Liga also recording better scoring rates than the English top flight.

The change is particularly striking when measured against the previous campaign.

Serie A averaged just 2.43 goals across the entirety of 2025-26, meaning its current scoring rate represents an increase of approximately 28%.

However, the transformation becomes even more dramatic when comparing the opening 110 matches of both seasons.

At the same stage last year, Italian clubs had managed just 2.22 goals per game. The latest figures therefore represent a rise of around 40%, raising questions about what has changed in a championship historically associated with defensive organisation.

The difference between the two seasons extends well beyond the overall number of goals.

According to figures compiled by Futbor, only two of Serie A's opening 110 matches this season have ended goalless, compared with 17 at the equivalent stage of 2025-26.

Meanwhile, 21 matches have produced at least five goals, and 60% of fixtures have featured three or more.

The Premier League has reached that three-goal threshold in just 47% of its opening 100 matches.

Italy's attacking revival has also been driven by several clubs rather than one exceptionally prolific team.

Gian Piero Gasperini's Roma lead the scoring charts with 31 goals in 11 matches, followed by defending champions Inter Milan with 28.

Lazio have contributed 25, while promoted Frosinone have scored 24, making them one of the most entertaining sides outside the traditional Italian elite.

The dramatic shift has produced several extraordinary results.

Inter defeated Udinese 5-3 in September, Atalanta drew 4-4 with Frosinone in October, and Lazio recorded a 6-2 away victory over Sassuolo later that month.

Roma also demonstrated their attacking strength with a 5-2 win at Udinese, reflecting the ambitious approach Gasperini has continued to develop since leaving Atalanta.

The contrast with English football is notable.

Arsenal currently lead the Premier League despite scoring only 15 goals in their first 10 matches, relying heavily on a defence that has conceded just five.

The Gunners' consistency illustrates that attacking productivity is not necessarily the determining factor in a successful championship campaign.

Nevertheless, the figures challenge the familiar perception that English football provides greater attacking entertainment than its Italian counterpart.

They also suggest that the recent transformation in Serie A deserves closer examination.

One explanation lies in the growing influence of coaches willing to adopt more aggressive approaches.

Gasperini has long been associated with intense man-to-man pressing, attacking wing-backs and a willingness to commit several players forward.

His influence, established during his successful spell at Atalanta, is now evident at Roma, who have become the division's most productive attacking side.

Cesc Fabregas has brought a different philosophy to Como.

The former Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder has built his team around possession, positional rotations and combinations designed to create numerical superiority in midfield.

Although Como's 18 goals in 11 matches fall below the league's most prolific sides, their approach demonstrates the variety of tactical ideas gaining ground in Italian football.

Cristian Chivu represents another example of the changing coaching landscape.

The former Chelsea defender guided Inter to the Serie A title in his first full season in charge and has continued to develop an attack-oriented approach with the reigning champions.

There is also evidence that these changes extend beyond the most recognisable managers.

Massimiliano Alvini's Frosinone have scored more than twice per match, despite operating with significantly fewer resources than Italy's biggest clubs.

Speaking to Italian newspaper Il Foglio, tactical analyst Adriano Bacconi reported that the number of attacking moves ending inside the opposition penalty area had increased by more than 20% compared with the previous season.

That figure offers a potential explanation for the scoring surge: teams are reaching dangerous areas more frequently, increasing the opportunities to create chances.

The greater emphasis on pressing and attacking numbers can also leave defences exposed during transitions.

Former AC Milan defender Filippo Galli suggested that changes in coaching philosophies have contributed to the increase, while acknowledging that modern defenders face increasingly complex responsibilities when building attacks from the back.

Those tactical developments do not mean that Italy's defensive traditions have disappeared.

Indeed, some of the additional goals may reflect defensive vulnerabilities rather than improved attacking quality alone.

The emergence of younger players offers another encouraging development.

Official Serie A figures highlighted that under-21 players had contributed 49 goals during the opening 10 matchdays, more than in any of Europe's other four major leagues.

Players such as Como's Nico Paz are benefiting from opportunities to assume significant attacking responsibilities, although the development of young talent does not automatically resolve the wider structural problems facing Italian football.

Financially, Serie A remains some distance behind the Premier League, and Italy's failure to qualify for three consecutive World Cups underlines the challenges facing the national game.

The early scoring figures also require perspective: 110 matches represent less than a third of the season, and the average could decline as the campaign progresses.

For now, however, the evidence is compelling.

Serie A has gone from averaging barely more than two goals per match at this stage last season to challenging the Bundesliga for European scoring supremacy.

Its revival suggests that Italian clubs are finding newly introduced ways to compete and entertain, even without the Premier League's financial resources.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 11:37 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 11:44 EST, 20 November 2026.

It has been revealed that derek McInnes can be understood in wanting a quiet January window. He’s still bonding a squad of players together. Drama and diversions are the last thing he needs when there looks to be an opportunity to win a title on the horizon.

In the case of Olwethu Makhanya, for example, this is definitely not the time to sell.

The 22-year-old South African has been impressive at centre-back, but it will take a campaign catching the attention in high-level European football for him to raise his value to Calvin Bassey levels and beyond.

Same goes for the likes of Ryan Naderi. Getting into the Czechia squad and increasing his range of experience makes him a more interesting prospect, but UEFA competition is a platform that ought to increase his premium.

McInnes, as he did this week, has to say he wants to keep his more prominent talents anyway. It would be strange to appear accepting of the board cashing in on bigger players.

Sources indicate that when it comes to Nico Raskin, however, things are different. A buyer for him should have been found in the summer after his World Cup involvement with Belgium.

Rangers midfielder Nico Raskin is an asset who could be sold in the January transfer window.

From the chit-chat around the game, it does not seem unreasonable to think Rangers maybe overvalued him in the initial part of that window and missed the boat in terms of securing a sale.

If he stays for the rest of this season and enters the final year of his contract, though, the money you can ask for naturally reduces. The club might seek to tie him up on a latest deal, of course, but his remarks about being ‘mentally ready to leave’ at the start of the season point to the most likely direction of travel.

Is he irreplaceable? Not at all. And this is where forward planning should come into the mix.

If there’s someone out there willing to edge anywhere close to the £15m mark for the 25-year-old, they should be getting sounded out now – with a contingency proposal being discussed and worked on in tandem.

Yes, Rangers need to get back to winning silverware, but the need to start raising funds through selling players – and replacing them - at appropriate times is pressing too.

As often remarked here, they can’t keep spending money the way they have been without considerably more coming back in return.

According to recent reports, raskin’s a good player, but his three-and-a-half years at Ibrox have hardly been shaped by his propensity for winning medals, have they? If a realistic fee is there in January, there’s a case to make for it being taken.

The Reds also switched to a back three with Ben Heneghan, Josh Flint and Charlie Barker, which provided the side with a lot of solidity.

When asked about his thought process around making that change to the formation, Blackwell remarked: “Well we haven’t kept many clean sheets have we.”.

The result justified the extra body he added to the defence to sure it up at the back and he was full of praise for the way his side defended.

It has been revealed that when faced with a follow up question regarding whether he will stick with this winning formula, Blackwell said: “I will look at all options. It depends on who we play against and how they play – that could have a big bearing on what we do.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the crisp chill of a late November evening in North Lanarkshire, Rangers required a late deflection to prise three vital Scottish Premiership points from the grasp of a resolute and industrious Motherwell side.

With the contest seemingly bound to end 1-1, a potentially significant blip for the visitors in terms of their title aspirations, Ryan Naderi’s 88th-minute effort struck the unfortunate Martin Moormann and looped past goalkeeper Alex Paulsen, inflicting the cruellest of blows on the Steelmen.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

There seemed an almost ritualistic rhythm to Rangers’ recent visits to Fir Park: waves of possession crashing against a disciplined claret-and-amber breakwater, accompanied by the persistent nagging doubt that dominance without ruthlessness invites punishment.

Derek McInnes’s side were living out that exact cautionary tale on their latest visit before Naderi popped up with a crucial late winner.

In a recent development, for the opening 15 minutes, this contest threatened to become a procession. Rangers monopolised the ball and the opening goal arrived after just eight minutes. Motherwell’s defensive structure momentarily frayed under early pressure, allowing centre-back Emmanuel Fernandez to rise unmarked and head home Kim Min-Su’s corner with disarming simplicity.

At that juncture, Motherwell appeared to be unravelling. Within six minutes of falling behind, Alfred Johansson was forced into an early reshuffle when winger Ibrahim Mentioned limped off injured in visible distress to be replaced by Regan Charles-Cook.

Recent findings suggest that rangers sensed blood. Naderi probed tirelessly, Djeidi Gassama repeatedly cut inside off the left flank to test the Steelmen defence, and Motherwell goalkeeper Alex Paulsen was called upon to produce a string of top-class saves to prevent the visitors from establishing an unassailable cushion.

Recent findings suggest that however, Scottish football rarely rewards aesthetic superiority alone. Having weathered the initial storm without conceding a second, the hosts summoned an equaliser from their first corner of the evening in the 21st minute. Emmanuel Longelo rolled a clever short pass to Tom Sparrow, whose curling delivery into the penalty area found Jake Girdwood-Reich entirely unmarked. The Australian defender needed no second invitation, sweeping a composed finish past Ivor Pandur to restore parity against the run of play.

That subtly altered the psychological temperature inside Fir Park. While Rangers continued to dictate proceedings, racking up nearly 20 attempts on goal, their lack of cutting edge in the final third was glaring. Before the interval, Paulsen defied the visitors once more with a superb reflex stop from Nico Raskin in the 41st minute.

McInnes’ men pressed forward with renewed urgency after a stern half-time team talk. Seven minutes into the second half, Dan Neil drifted into a pocket of space on the edge of the area and drilled a low effort that whistled agonisingly past the post.

Visible frustration began to creep into Rangers’ ranks passing the hour mark as a combination of misplaced passes and poor finishing drew audible groans from the packed away end.

Recent findings suggest that sensing his team’s grip on the contest loosening, McInnes turned to his bench in the 69th minute, introducing summer signing Kevin Kelsy in place of Gassama to add a greater physical presence in attack alongside Naderi. There was little immediate improvement. Badredine Bouanani raced down the right flank and cut the ball back for Neil, whose shot sailed high and wide.

Motherwell were looking increasingly comfortable and Tawanda Maswanhise tested Pandur from distance as the home side sensed an opportunity to claim something more substantial than a point.

Findlay Curtis was introduced for Rangers and almost made an immediate impact, delivering an excellent cross towards the back post which Naderi was unable to turn home from close range.

According to recent reports, then came another extraordinary intervention from Paulsen. Curtis' effort appeared to have beaten the keeper, who could only palm the ball into the path of Sterling. However, Paulsen recovered magnificently to divert the right-back’s follow-up onto the crossbar. It was a remarkable piece of goalkeeping and, by this stage, it seemed entirely possible that the home side would clinch a share of the spoils.

They were not to be so fortunate.

With two minutes remaining, Rangers finally found the breakthrough their territorial dominance had threatened to deliver. Naderi got his effort away, but Moormann intervened and inadvertently diverted the ball beyond his own goalkeeper. The unfortunate centre-back could do little about the decisive deflection, but the consequences were devastating for Motherwell.

The travelling Rangers support erupted, relief and celebration combining in equal measure. For McInnes, it was a precious late reward for a side that had made unnecessarily hard work of a match they might have settled long before the closing stages.

The victory extends Rangers' unbeaten run in all competitions to 13 matches and ensures they remain in touch with Celtic, moving back within four points of the league leaders with a game in hand.

Formation tweak and a monkey off their back - Five things we learned from Crawley Town's substantial win over Fleetwood

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that there was a drastic change in formation as the Reds moved to a back three with Ben Heneghan in the middle of the back three with Josh Flint and Charlie Barker either side.
  • Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.
  • Playing two strikers from the very start is something fans have been crying out for with it being a rarity this season for two strikers to start from the outset with the Reds typically bringing on a second striker towards the end of a game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Here are five things we learned.

Industry observers note that there was a drastic change in formation as the Reds moved to a back three with Ben Heneghan in the middle of the back three with Josh Flint and Charlie Barker either side. Blackwell also decided to field an extra striker with Pemi Aderoju and Danilo Orsi leading the line.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Playing two strikers from the very start is something fans have been crying out for with it being a rarity this season for two strikers to start from the outset with the Reds typically bringing on a second striker towards the end of a game.

It evidently paid off not just in terms of the result but the performance. Orsi is a player who needs service; he isn’t a target man and he isn’t someone whose strong suit is running in behind, so having Aderoju alongside him only compliments him and ultimately brings the best out of each other's game, especially if Crawley continue to play direct.

This win over Fleetwood is Crawley’s first home league since Colin Kazim-Richards first game in charge at the end of March, which was eight months ago.

According to recent reports, to hang on to that lead at the end was crucial. Having not had a home league win this season, that would have played on the minds of the players and it was certainly felt in the crowd.

But to now overcome that hurdle, the Reds can really look to make the Broadfield Stadium a fortress going forward.

The Reds seemed to have a lot more fight with a real intensity to the way they played, an element of their game which Blackwell alluded to in his post-match interview also.

They had a lot of time to prepare for today’s game having had no game last weekend, and so that would have allowed not only more time to work on tactical elements of the game, but also their fitness and sharpness and that certainly came across today.

The Reds won a lot of their aerial duels and were convincing in their tackles and challenges across the pitch, showing a real togetherness amongst the players who were all fighting for each other out on that pitch, which is crucial if they want to get out of the position they are in.

Unbeaten run in the league continues.

Not only was it Crawley’s first home league win of the season, but it also continued their unbeaten run in the league since Blackwell arrived. It started with a 1-1 draw against Tranmere Rovers before a 0-1 win on the road against Oldham Athletic.

Something which Blackwell has reiterated in a number of interviews is full focus on the league, and that focus has proven itself in the results and now it’s all about keeping that run going and building momentum.

The Reds looked very well organised and structured both in and out of position, rarely being caught out in the transition. Blackwell’s teams over the years have been known for being disciplined and cohesive, and that is starting to show in this Crawley side who defended very resolutely in today’s games.

Particularly with the way Crawley have played under Blackwell, they won’t dominate large proportions of the games and today was a prime example.

Both teams had different spells of pressure and dominance throughout the game, with Crawley being the ones to capitalise with two early goals at the start of each half.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Derek McInnes labelled Ryan Naderi “a substantial horse” and a textbook example of how to lead the line as a centre-forward after helping Rangers secure a hard-fought 2-1 Premiership victory over Motherwell.

The German striker has been growing in confidence in recent weeks and once again demonstrated his importance to the Ibrox side, combining tireless pressing and intelligent movement which resulted in a scrappy late 88th-minute winner at Fir park.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

McInnes believes Naderi's contribution extends far beyond his goals, insisting his work rate should not overshadow the quality of his all-round performances.

“Ryan’s game is really strong at the minute. He looks like a very confident boy and so he should be,” McInnes remarked. “Wrongly now, when you think of Ryan or people ask me, it’s about him knocking his pan in. His pressing is unbelievable and he’s a big horse up there. He runs and works and puts people under pressure.

Recent findings suggest that “He looks tired but his performances are always strong. But he gets goals and has an influence. In that system tonight, his was the most notable position for us, in terms of running channels and getting hold of the ball. His touch was one of a really confident player and he led the line brilliantly. It was a proper number nine performance.”.

Sources indicate that on his side’s performance, McInnes added: “We got our just rewards in the game, absolutely. I thought it was a very good, strong performance and I’ve been told that every one of my outfield players had a shot tonight. I’ve never known a team who practice so much shooting, and crossing and finishing during the week.

Recent findings suggest that “It was the only thing missing for us, I thought it was a top class performance. We mixed the game up well. Our press was strong and we were aggressive. I’m just disappointed it took so long to get the winning goal.”.

Deflated Motherwell boss Alfred Johansson admitted his side struggled to cope with Rangers' early intensity, but felt the early loss of Ibrahim Stated to injury was a major blow before his side ran out of energy in the closing stages.

In a recent development, “They are title challengers and we have a really tough start to the game,” he mentioned. “They put us down. When we win it back, we give it away again. They get momentum. I don't think it's a free kick that they get before their first goal, but we should defend much, much better on that defensive corner kick.

In a recent development, “In that moment, in the same period, we lose Ibrahim [Noted], which is really tough for us, given that the players we have on the bench, many of them in the offensive positions, are not ready to play more than 30 to 45 minutes with high intensity. So it was tough to lose him, and therefore, it's strong of the players to come back and score a goal from a set play and equalise.

“But the last 15-20 minutes, Rangers take completely over and we don't have energy enough in that moment to keep the intensity up.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 20 Nov 2026 17:58.

David Moyes has provided the latest enhancement on Jack Grealish’s availability ahead of Everton’s Premier League trip to Brentford on Monday.

The Manchester City loanee was dropped from the Toffees squad ahead of last month’s EFL Cup victory over Newcastle United for what was described as a “breach of club discipline".

In his absence, Everton enjoyed a strong run of form, securing victories against Newcastle in both the cup and the Premier League, as well as a top-flight win over Coventry City.

It is understood that Grealish he was deemed unfit for all three games after missing training sessions, while he was also unavailable for the defeat at Arsenal in October due to illness.

To help rebuild his sharpness alongside midfielder Christian Norgaard ahead of the trip to the Gtech Community Stadium, Everton arranged a friendly against Derby County at Hill Dickinson Stadium, in which Grealish took part.

Following that outing, the England international took to Instagram to issue a public statement apologising to “the fans and everyone at the club for not being able to help the team the last few weeks”.

Speaking at a pre-match press conference on Friday, Moyes confirmed that Grealish is now available for first-team selection, telling reporters: “He’s back in training and in and around the team.

In a recent development, “I don’t do social media but I’ve heard about it (the apology). We’ve just been getting on with our work. We’ve got a lot of other players here who I need to focus on as well.

Sources indicate that “I can’t just concentrate on one player. I’ve been trying to make sure everyone has got the right preparation for Brentford.”.

It remains to be seen whether Grealish will be thrown straight back into the starting lineup, or whether Tyrique George will retain his place on the left wing.

Grealish is yet to score or assist in eight appearances for Everton across all competitions this season and his long-term future with the club remains uncertain, with both his Toffees loan deal and Man City contract expiring in June next year.

Meanwhile, Moyes has confirmed that he is set to have a fully-fit Everton squad for the trip to Brentford.

Sources indicate that “Yeah, I believe [we have a fully fit squad],” stated the Scotsman. “We’ve not had anyone return back from international duty with any problems.

“We’ve got another few days to go before we get to game day so hopefully we won’t pick up any.”.

The Toffees boss added that Norgaard is "coming back to a level of fitness" and "is getting closer" to being able to make a start for the club, but a place in the first XI against his former side Brentford seems unlikely.

Moyes, who will break Harry Catterick's record of 592 games in charge of Everton, at the moment sees him team sitting sixth in the Premier League table, two points above Brentford in eighth place.

Latest Update: England throw it away with defending unworthy of a top nation

⏱️ ~32 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, there had been so much talk – first raised by Thomas Tuchel after the shocking World Cup exit to Argentina – about England’s DNA.
  • It has been revealed that the world and European champions were England’s first opponents – after the World Cup – in this Nations League campaign and came away from Wembley with a deserved win.
  • It has been revealed that mikel Oyarzabal SCORES against England AGAIN!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, there had been so much talk – first raised by Thomas Tuchel after the shocking World Cup exit to Argentina – about England’s DNA. About whether they could keep the ball, pass the ball, control the ball, the way Spain do.

It has been revealed that the world and European champions were England’s first opponents – after the World Cup – in this Nations League campaign and came away from Wembley with a deserved win. They are now 39 games unbeaten with substitute Mikel Oyarzabal, who scored the winning goal against England in the final of the last European Championship, doing so again.

It has been revealed that mikel Oyarzabal SCORES against England AGAIN! 🎯Spain retake the lead after a slick finish from the Spaniard 👏#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pPT3KvRHWl.

Recent findings suggest that that may have been no surprise, even if the inevitable “olés” after Spain’s third goal will have hurt. But the nature of it? For the England manager this was another shocker. Not in the way his team went about the task. They were positive, fun, attacking. But in the way they conceded – goals and chances – and lost.

Recent findings suggest that on this performance, DNA, for England, stands for Defensively Not Able, as they threw away what could have been a famous and restorative victory. Instead, with Croatia beating the Czech Republic in the other group game, England are under immediate pressure to win in Prague on Tuesday.

In a recent development, in fact, England have conceded 13 goals in their past six matches – in fairness including four in that third-place World Cup 6-4 win over France – and that is not good enough for a top-tier nation. Tuchel needs to sort it out defensively.

Sources indicate that it could have been very different if Harry Kane had not missed from the penalty spot, slipping as he struck the ball, with England improbably 2-1 ahead. “It would have been the decisive punch,” Tuchel stated. Maybe so, even if there was always the feeling that Spain could go through the gears.

Sources indicate that kane MISSES from the penalty spot! 😧Harry Kane slips when he strikes the ball, let off for Spain and Luis de la Fuente#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pvg3GGa9ma.

Afterwards there were claims, led by the impressive Anthony Gordon, that this was a missed opportunity for England. A bit like the World Cup. They need to shake this theme.

Sources indicate that the irony was this was one of their best creative displays for quite some time. They took the game to Spain and could have scored more. And conceded more.

In truth it could have been Spain 4 England 0 inside half an hour and before Tuchel’s team laid a glove on their opponents.

Another let off for England 😧Ferran Torres misses another massive chance one-on-one with James Trafford #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/KFkJoJUW6c.

Sources indicate that the manager had also spoken about how England should “embrace the chaos” as their best route to success. That may appear a questionable tactic – does chaos ever win a tournament? – but England certainly did that. This was as chaotic and, admittedly, entertaining as it gets.

Recent findings suggest that england attacked with pace and power with the pick of their players the two based in Spain: Gordon, who scored, and Jude Bellingham. And the defenders? This was a bad night for Marc Guéhi, his Manchester City team-mate Nico O’Reilly (cue speculation about whether they were distracted by the verdict on the Premier League charges against their club) and for Jarell Quansah at right-back who is so evidently a centre-half.

A penny, once more, for the thoughts of the unused Trent Alexander-Arnold. The fourth defender, Ezri Konsa, vented his frustration at what was happening around him.

It was not just the errors but the unforced nature of them. Poor in possession with misplaced passes and defensively wide open. There is a gap between Spain and England but not as big as the gaps that were exposed in England’s back four. They endured a full house of calamities. They seemed strangely unaware – or incapable of dealing with – the danger posed by the outstanding Lamine Yamal.

Industry observers note that maybe because of the opposition – or the criticism – England felt the need to play out. But what an horrific start. What an inexplicable moment for Guéhi as he received the ball from O’Reilly and turned into trouble, gifting possession to Yamal who ran on and scored. Inside two minutes.

WHAT A START FROM SPAIN 🇪🇸Lamine Yamal pounces on a Marc Guéhi error to give Spain an early lead at Wembley #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/Et83EyTPlp.

Recent findings suggest that spain walked out with the second star on their shirt – to mark their second World Cup triumph. That was the star Tuchel had promised for England.

According to recent reports, now, straight away, they were up against it. It could have turned very ugly. Ferran Torres, who had scored the winner in the World Cup Final, had one disallowed for offside, then was thwarted by James Trafford after – inexplicably again – being played onside by Quansah.

SUBSTANTIAL SAVE from James Trafford 🧤The Leeds United goalkeeper keeps out Ferran Torres#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/nj5b8AUSQU.

It has been revealed that then Torres was sent clear following Elliot Anderson’s poor pass, only to drag his shot wide. The third miss came from Dani Olmo, again set up by Yamal.

Industry observers note that it could – it should – have been game over. Then England unexpectedly turned it around. They had kept attacking despite what was going on at the back and struck through a truly thrilling counter-attack, with Gordon and Bellingham combining before the Barcelona winger calmly beat goalkeeper Unai Simon.

ENGLAND ARE LEVEL! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿A brilliant finish from Anthony Gordon after a breathtaking counter attack 👏#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/z0nSfWIHVd.

It was an exceptional goal and was quickly followed by a fortunate one as O’Reilly’s cross was met by Kane who stooped to steer in a header, only for it to strike Marc Cucurella, who made a mess of clearing, and it went past Simón.

I think we'll give that goal to Harry Kane 🎯England come from behind to lead Spain thanks Harry Kane, with assistance from Marc Cucurella ⚽️#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/X3qSOWUhVT.

The Spain left-back hit the post with a cross, misjudged by Trafford who was given this game and the next to stake his claim ahead of Jordan Pickford who has so long been the undisputed first-choice.

England dominated for a while and Bellingham won a penalty, after a VAR intervention, only for Kane to strike the crossbar.

How Spain made them pay and worryingly so. O’Reilly passed the ball straight to Olmo who swept it inside. Substitute Álex Baena checked and beat Trafford from the edge of the area. Even worse was how Spain cut through the heart of England defence with Baena finding Oyarzabal. Why was no defender closer to him? What was Guéhi doing? And O’Reilly? Oyarzabal exquisitely dinked the ball over Trafford.

Thomas Tuchel does not think Manchester City’s guilty verdict over almost all of their Premier League charges distracted his England players in the Nations League defeat to Spain.

City players Marc Guéhi and Nico O’Reilly were at fault for two of Spain’s goals and both Tuchel, the head coach, and England captain Harry Kane confirmed news of the verdict had been discussed among the squad.

Tuchel does not plan to address the concern with his players ahead of the remaining Nations League games against Czech Republic and Croatia.

Asked if the City verdict had been a cause of discussion ahead of the Spain game, Tuchel replied: “Not for me, but I can imagine maybe for the Man City players. I won’t comment on it as it’s an ongoing case.

“I didn’t make it a topic. It was not a topic for me. I’m just thinking about Spain and the team and meetings. The players have more time than me. So I can imagine they talk about it. It’s good they do. I don’t think it was a distraction for them.”.

Kane added: “There was a discussion, but when we’re with England, we kind of put club football to one side and it was no different this week.”.

Tuchel also refused to point the finger of blame at Guéhi, O’Reilly or Kane, who missed a penalty, for England’s defeat despite admitting his team got off to the worst possible start by conceding a goal after two minutes.

“We will focus on the positives, but also highlight the stuff we can do better,” Tuchel said. “Not even speaking about individual mistakes because this is normal. It just happens. It should not happen, and for sure not in this amount. But there is no sense in showing the individual mistakes or telling them ‘please don’t make mistakes’. That is normal, but we can do things better. We can defend the third goal better. But we will focus on the positives. There is a lot to take away from the game.

“We wanted to be the team desperately to beat them [Spain] and we think we had them. We still think we had them at half-time. That was the way the team demonstrated up after half-time. So we will focus on that, but the reality is we lost and the reality is we need to prove it again.”.

It has been revealed that “It was a terrible start, the worst possible start, which makes it so difficult against a team like this. The reaction was very good. After 10/12 minutes, we were the better team but we gave away too many mistakes. We were the better team. If we had converted the penalty, it could have been the decisive moment. We have to keep going and learn from the mistakes. We could have created more if we had been more clinical in the final 20 metres. We revealed great bravery and courage with our high-ball wins. There will always be moments you suffer against teams like this. The effort and quality were there tonight but the result does not prove it today.”.

According to recent reports, “I think there is a gap [between Spain and England]. They [Spain] are the world champions and European champions. Mikel Oyarzabal was never going to miss. He was always in control of the situation. Honestly, people talk about sexy football, that is sexy football. I would watch that all night.”.

🗣️ "We went toe to toe with the European and world champions" 💪Harry Kane remains positive about England performance despite their 3-2 defeat to Spain 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿🇪🇸#ITVFootball | @gabrielclarke05 | @England pic.twitter.com/qkhqsqmPEl.

🗣️ "You have to beat them to show people we can do this" 💪@IanWright0 reflects on England's 3-2 defeat to Spain at Wembley#ITVFootball | @markpougatch pic.twitter.com/ko2FYs4VqA.

Industry observers note that marc Guehi and Nico O’Reilly may want to look away now but Jude Bellingham and Anthony Gordon scored well. Our very own Mike McGrath has provided his player ratings.

A highly entertaining game. England will probably argue the game changed on Kane’s missed penalty, but Spain missed a lot of very clear chances and will feel they deserved the victory. A losing start to the Nations League for Tuchel and his team, but there were some positives. Gordon, Bellingham and Anderson were all excellent. Some of the defending, not so excellent.

They’ve missed a couple of one-on-ones, hit the post and blazed over the bar. Highly entertaining and England will know they will have to defend better if they are going to hold on to their lead.

An absorbing and end-to-end first half is brought to an end. Somehow, despite the fact at one point they could have been 3-0 down, England lead 2-1 at the break.

Cucurella’s cross from the left loops all the way to the back post, where it strikes the frame of the goal. I do not think Cucurella meant that.

England gift the ball away so poorly and Yamal should punish them with his second goal of the game but he blazes high over the bar.

Harry Kane wants England to address how they lost their identity and went “against our beliefs” at the World Cup.

In a brutally honest assessment of the tournament, the England captain admitted Thomas Tuchel’s team did not play to their full potential in several games – even before the painful semi-final exit against Argentina.

Kane, who played golf instead of watching the World Cup final, revealed the 2-1 Atlanta defeat hurt more than missing a penalty four years earlier in Qatar, when England were knocked out by France in the quarter-finals.

“This one hurt more than any other one. I would probably say even more than when I missed a penalty in Qatar because of the manner that it happened,” Kane said. “It was not us as a team.

“We trust our players and the player know very well that if you miss a camp then someone plays well in your position that the competition is always on. You have to make sure to be available and to produce top-level performances in camp and if you do so, that counts for something. Right now, it is not on my list of worries. I am not wired like this. From the moment I arrived at SGP my full focus is 100 per cent with the players who are here.

Industry observers note that “There is no threat, distrust or threat of consequences. It will come naturally. I truly believe that we have the opposite. You will talk to our captain, Harry Kane, who has the most minutes for club and country and is happy to be here while teammates of his are enjoying a 10-day break. He is the role model and that is the vibe we have here.”.
