According to recent reports, a, A diagram illustrating our non-magnetic behavioural rig for monitoring trajectories of tethered flying moths. The panorama-walled flight arena, enclosed within three-dimensional Helmholtz coils (coil outer dimensions: X: 1245 mm, Y: 1300 mm, Z: 700 mm), receives dorsal projections of a starry night sky (generated using Stellarium) on a UV-transparent Perspex circular lid topped with a UV-transmissive diffuser (Lee Filter 251, 1/4 white). This lid was placed on top of the arena and optic flow was ventrally projected onto a similarly constructed screen installed below the moth, under the arena. An optical encoder, mounted at the centre of the lid, and connected to the moth via a non-magnetic tungsten rod (g), records instantaneous flight headings every 200 ms. The ventral optic flow is synchronised via feedback with the moth’s real-time heading using Mapflow.exe software, ensuring that flow direction is always nose-to-tail irrespective of the moth’s heading. b, The projected natural starry sky at 21:30 on 15 October 2022 during the Bogong moth’s southward spring migration. c, The projected randomised starry sky. Top-view (d) and moth’s-eye view (e) of the panoramic “landscape” scene within the arena. f, A flying moth with a tungsten stalk seen from the front (wing flapping envelope visible). g, The optic flow projected beneath the moth (shown at much greater intensity than used in experiments, for the sake of visibility).

a1–a4, The orientations of moths (light blue vectors) captured during both spring migrations (2023: α = 231°, n = 57, R* = 1.675, p = 6.5 × 10−3, CI95 = 195°-268°; 2024: α = 214°, n = 65, R* = 1.532, p = 0.024, CI95 = 174°-254°) and both autumn migrations (2024: α = 17°, n = 62, R* = 1.179, p = 0.408, CI95 = 319°-75° and 2025: α = 18°, n = 64, R* = 1.729, p = 3.8 × 10−3, CI95 = 342°-53°). Moths were flown in a panorama-walled arena and were exposed to a dorsal projection of a full-spectrum randomised starry sky and a natural (0°: NMF 0) geomagnetic field (generated by 3-dimensional Helmholtz coils). b1–b4, Spring and autumn moths (light blue vectors) subjected to the same conditions as in a1–a4 except with the geomagnetic field (and magnetic north) rotated by 180° (NMF 180) (2023 spring: α = 44°, n = 62, R* = 2.388, p = 1.4 × 10−6, CI95 = 19°-69°; 2024 spring: α = 16°, n = 66, R* = 1.916, p = 5.0 × 10−4, CI95 = 345°-47°; 2024 autumn: α = 229°, n = 65, R* = 1.58, p = 0.016, CI95 = 190°-268°; 2025 autumn: α = 217°, n = 67, R* = 2.249, p = 8.6 × 10−6, CI95 = 191°-243°). c1–c4, The orientation directions of migratory moths (light blue vectors) experiencing a randomised starry sky and a nulled magnetic field during both springs (2023: n = 49, R* = 0.471, p = 0.524; 2024: n = 73, R* = 0.281, p = 0.793) and both autumns (2024: n = 65, R* = 0.167, p = 0.921; 2025: n = 59, R* = 0.194, p = 0.896). d1–d4, The orientation directions of migratory moths (orange vectors) in a natural (0°) geomagnetic field, but this time experiencing randomised stars whose light spectrum had been filtered to exclude UV-blue light (λ > 500 nm) during both springs (2023: n = 51, R* = 0.295, p = 0.776; 2024: n = 55, R* = 0.42, p = 0.598) and both autumns (2024: n = 54, R* = 0.582, p = 0.372; 2025: n = 61, R* = 0.277, p = 0.799). In all panels, each red mean vector (red arrow) results from weighting the mean directions and mean directedness (vector lengths) of all of the individual moths, as analysed by a one-sided Moore’s modified Rayleigh test (MMRT), with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons. The direction and directedness of mean vectors is given by α and R*, respectively. The dashed circles show the required R* value for statistical significance: p < 0.05, p < 0.01 and p < 0.001, respectively for increasing radius. The shaded areas show the 95% confidence intervals (CI95). mN, magnetic north.

a, A schematic “map” of the spatial arrangement of two parallel-operated flight simulators controlled from computers located in a black light-tight cubical tent (connecting cables shown as blue wavy lines). b, Spectral transmission measurements (irradiance) under natural stellar illumination for the four arenas: Clear Arena (1 layer of Lee filter 130, λ > 310 nm), Clear-ND Arena (1 layer of Lee filter 130 and 1 layer of 0.9 ND Lee filter 211, λ > 310 nm), UV-blocking Arena (2 layers of Lee filter 226, λ > 380 nm), and UV-blue-blocking Arena (2 layers of Lee filter 226 and 1 layer of Lee filter 768, λ > 500 nm). The measurement cut-off below Log Irradiance = 5 coincided with measurement noise in the detector (Ocean Optics QE65PRO Spectrometer). c, The experimental protocol for exploring the illumination spectral bands required for geomagnetic compass orientation in Bogong moths (in the drawings of the arena, please note the cardboard disk placed on the encoder stalk above the moth to block its view of the night sky, and thus disable its stellar compass). In experiments 1 and 2, two cohorts of ca. 20 moths were flown in parallel in each of two arenas in Phase 1 and then swapped to the other arena in Phase 2 to repeat the experiment. This controlled for the possibility that landscape landmarks seen from within each of the two arenas influenced the orientation of moths (which it did not). In experiment 3, a cohort of ca. 40 moths was flown in an arena with full spectrum illumination (λ > 310 nm) but reduced in intensity by ca. 8 times by a 0.9 log unit neutral density (ND) filter sheeting. This experiment controlled for the possibility that the intensity-reducing effect of the spectral filtering used in experiments 1 and 2 influenced the orientation of moths (which it did not).

In a recent development, a,c, In a Clear Arena (λ > 310 nm), Bogong moths (grey vectors) were oriented in their inherited migratory direction in both phases of experiment 1 (Phase 1, a1: α = 13°, n = 60, R* = 1.291, p = 0.136, CI95 = 321°-63°; Phase 2, a2: α = 34°, n = 45, R* = 1.339, p = 0.085, CI95 = 345°-82°) and in both phases of experiment 2 (Phase 1, c1: α = 24°, n = 61, R* = 1.548, p = 0.015, CI95 = 343°-63°; Phase 2, c2: α = 14°, n = 61, R* = 1.59, p = 0.010, CI95 = 335°-53°). b, In a UV-blocking Arena (λ > 380 nm), moths (light purple vectors) were also oriented in their inherited migratory direction in both phases of experiment 1 (Phase 1, b1: α = 21°, n = 49, R* = 1.391, p = 0.068, CI95 = 335°-67°; Phase 2, b2: α = 27°, n = 42, R* = 1.274, p = 0.153, CI95 = 335°-79°). d, In a UV-blue-blocking Arena (λ > 500 nm), moths (light orange vectors) were disoriented in both phases of experiment 2 (Phase 1, d1: n = 58, R* = 0.36, p = 0.685; Phase 2, d2: n = 54, R* = 0.345, p = 0.707). Other Fig. conventions as in Extended Data Fig. 2.

According to recent reports, a,b, A photo of an antenna made of coaxial cable. The antenna is placed around the outside wall of the flight simulator arena and connected to a signal and waveform generator (Rigol DG 1022U) via a BNC port. c, Measurements of the magnetic components of the RF fields at 2.5 Vpp (RF ON - red), 0.04 mVpp (Minimum - magenta), the generator turned off (Background - blue), and the generator in stand-by mode (RF OFF - yellow). Average (RMS: root-mean-square; left column) and “maxhold” (maximum intensity; right column) measurements are shown for the frequency range up to 100 MHz (top row) and up to 300 MHz (bottom row) to demonstrate the absence of off-target harmonics. The respective density and intensity values are listed in Extended Data Table 3.

Magnetic fields were generated via a three-dimensional Helmholtz coil system and measured (in nanotesla, nT) six times over 300 s, yielding X, Y, and Z traces. Traces were averaged to compute mean component strengths (X, Y, Z: red, green, blue lines) with standard deviations (shaded regions). a1–a3, The three-component vector of a natural geomagnetic field (NMF0) at 0° azimuth. b1–b3, The three-component vector of NMF0 at 0° azimuth with an imposed 2.5 Vpp (volts peak-to-peak) radio frequency (RF) field (NMF0 + RF_2.5VPP). c1–c3, The three-component vector of a natural geomagnetic field rotated by 180° (NMF180). d1–d3, The three-component vector of a nulled geomagnetic field. e1–e3, The three-component vector of a natural geomagnetic field with inclination inverted. f1–f3, The three-component vector of a natural geomagnetic field with polarity inverted.

The illumination was provided by the projector (LED projector ASUS S1 Mobile) and a ring of 8 UV-emitting LEDs (LED370E Ultra Bright Deep Violet LED, Thorlabs) centred around the projector’s front lens. To manipulate the intensity and spectral composition of light entering the flight arena, we employed filter sheets (Lee Filters, USA) placed in front of the projector lens. For full spectrum illumination (purple curve), Neutral Density (ND) filters (Lee Filters 210, ND 0.6 log units and transmitting λ > 310 nm) were used to attenuate light intensity uniformly across all wavelengths (λ > 310 nm), preserving spectral integrity. Six layers of Lee Filter 210 were used to reduce illumination levels to natural stellar intensities (purple curve). For this spectrum (and during full-spectrum experiments), the ring of UV-emitting LEDS was turned ON). Lee Filter 768 (Egg Yolk Yellow) is a spectral long-pass filter that allows transmission of light from around 500 nm. To block the UV-violet-blue part of the illumination spectrum, and to maintain approximately the same starlight illumination intensity, 1 layer of Egg Yolk Yellow filter (Lee Filter 768, λ > 500 nm) and 5 layers of 0.6 ND filter (Lee Filters 210) were placed in front of the projector lens (orange curve). For this spectrum (and during the λ > 500 nm experiments), the ring of UV-emitting LEDS was turned OFF). Upward illumination intensity and spectrum measurements of the projected starry night sky were made from within the arena using an Ocean Optics QE65PRO Spectrometer (Ocean Optics) located underneath the projection screen at the position of the moth. The measurement cut-off below Log Irradiance = 5 coincided with measurement noise in the detector.

Supplementary Methods, including Supplementary Fig. 1 and Table 1.

Mikel Arteta shuts down Arsenal team news loophole exposed by Christos Tzolis

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (851 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 20 Nov 2026 18:48.
  • Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has confirmed that new measures have been introduced to prevent players from accidentally revealing confidential team news through Fantasy Premier League (FPL).
  • The decision follows an incident involving Christos Tzolis, whose selections in the popular fantasy football game offered an unexpected insight into his availability ahead of Arsenal's Premier League victory over Liverpool earlier this month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 20 Nov 2026 18:48.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has confirmed that new measures have been introduced to prevent players from accidentally revealing confidential team news through Fantasy Premier League (FPL).

The decision follows an incident involving Christos Tzolis, whose selections in the popular fantasy football game offered an unexpected insight into his availability ahead of Arsenal's Premier League victory over Liverpool earlier this month.

According to The Athletic, Arsenal players have been banned from selecting themselves or their teammates in their FPL squads, reducing the risk of injuries and potential starting line-ups being disclosed before official announcements.

Arteta confirmed the intervention during Friday's press conference ahead of Saturday's trip to Newcastle United, stressing that protecting information about his squad was essential to maintaining trust within the club.

The development is particularly interesting given that Sports Mole was among the outlets to highlight Tzolis's revealing Fantasy Premier League decisions before Arsenal's visit to Anfield on November 1.

Tzolis had been sidelined for approximately a month with a hamstring injury, missing six consecutive Arsenal matches before the trip to Liverpool.

Although Arteta had confirmed that the Greek international had returned to training, his involvement at Anfield remained uncertain.

However, the winger provided a significant indication of his fitness through his own Fantasy Premier League account.

Tzolis transferred himself into his team and selected himself as captain, effectively doubling the points he would earn if he made a successful return.

The decision attracted attention because fantasy managers generally avoid selecting injured players, particularly when using the captaincy on an individual who might not feature.

Sports Mole had already identified the potential significance of those choices in its November 1 report on Tzolis's Fantasy Premier League injury clues.

The same report noted that the former Norwich City winger had retained Riccardo Calafiori in his fantasy squad despite the defender also facing questions over his fitness.

Both players subsequently started at Anfield, where Arsenal secured a 1-0 victory.

Tzolis's activity attracted further attention in the following gameweek.

Ahead of Arsenal's home meeting with Hull City on November 7, the 24-year-old reportedly activated his wildcard, allowing him to make unlimited transfers, and removed every Arsenal player from his fantasy team.

Among those transferred out were Tzolis himself, Calafiori and Ezri Konsa.

Those decisions did not establish who would or would not start against Hull, but they demonstrated how closely players' fantasy activity could be monitored for potential clues.

Tzolis has also previously spoken openly about his enthusiasm for the game.

After Arsenal's opening-day victory over Coventry City, he discussed the points he had accumulated through his own performance, revealing that he had selected himself as captain.

What initially appeared to be a harmless aspect of the player's enjoyment of football has now prompted a response from his manager.

Asked whether he had addressed the issue with his players, Arteta confirmed that discussions had taken place involving Tzolis and other members of the squad.

"With Christos, with the squad and with my kids as well," the Arsenal manager remarked.

"They're constantly asking me about this as well, because they want to know. It's a topic.".

Arteta acknowledged that the popularity of Fantasy Premier League had created a relatively new challenge for clubs seeking to protect information about their players.

"These are the kind of things that are happening in our society right now," he explained.

"It's something new. We haven't dealt with it before and we need to put new things in place.".

The Spaniard then emphasised the importance of maintaining confidentiality within the dressing room and coaching staff.

"The confidentiality is something critical because it's about trust and what you're trying to do, and that should be kept as a huge secret.".

Arteta added that measures would be taken to prevent further incidents and subsequently confirmed that restrictions were already in place.

The reported policy does not prevent Arsenal players from participating in Fantasy Premier League altogether.

Instead, it specifically targets the selection of Arsenal footballers in their own fantasy teams, limiting the possibility that transfers or captaincy choices reveal information unavailable to opponents and supporters.

Arsenal are not the first Premier League club to confront the problem.

Chelsea faced similar concerns in October after fantasy accounts associated with players and staff appeared to offer clues about Joao Pedro's injury before his absence against Tottenham Hotspur became public.

The Brazilian had reportedly been removed from several fantasy teams ahead of that fixture, prompting speculation about his availability.

Chelsea subsequently warned staff about the risks of revealing confidential information through the game.

For Arsenal, the problem is especially relevant as Arteta attempts to maintain his side's position at the top of the Premier League.

The Gunners travel to Newcastle on Saturday with a five-point advantage over their nearest challengers, and the manager will be keen to avoid giving opponents unnecessary information about his selection decisions.

Tzolis's fantasy activity may have provided an early indication of his return against Liverpool, but Arsenal's new restrictions are designed to ensure that future team news emerges through official channels rather than virtual football transfers.

Industry observers note that “We have some examples here who joined us too late after pre-season, then you start to play,” acknowledged Jakirovic. “(You pick up) one injury, recovery, second injury. Now it's difficult to get back into the team – especially the first XI.

According to recent reports, “They need time and they have to be patient and work very hard every day. So this is risky.”.

Nobel Mendy is fit again after an international break where Hull had a large number of players representing their countries, and Jakirovic watching closely to see how they performed.

Industry observers note that “We had 12 players in the building (during the break),” he said. “But we had two good sessions before Thursday when we were finally all together. everyone got back healthy.

“Now it's about fatigue, it's about condition. On Saturday we will decide who will play.

“I tried to watch every game (his internationals played) and if I cannot watch, Josh (Marris, senior analyst) will put it on our computer. Even Qatar v Australia (which centre-back Lucas Herrington played in), even under-21 games, Greece, Norway, with Jens (Hjerto-Dahl).”.

Leeds United avenged the two cup defeats they suffered at Chelsea’s hands with a stunning 4-1 victory over their old rivals at Stamford Bridge.

Having been edged out by the Blues at the semi-final stage of the FA Cup in April, Leeds were subjected to a 6-3 Carabao Cup mauling by Xabi Alonso’s men in September.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Sources indicate that on this occasion, however, it was Daniel Farke’s men inflicting the damage. Emmanuel Emegha fired the hosts ahead, but Noah Okafor goals either side of a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty and a late Brenden Aaronson finish gave Leeds a Premier League win that will go down in the history books.

Chelsea sought to assume authority from the get-go, with Cole Palmer driving at the heart of the Leeds midfield inside the opening minute. The hosts may have been straight on the offensive, but Leeds soon made it clear they would not be content with one-way traffic.

Jayden Bogle and Sean Longstaff both made headway down the right-hand side, sending in crosses that were not capitalised upon.

The opening exchanges played out in a fast and furious manner, with robust challenges stoking the fires of a historic rivalry. Chelsea had the early edge, although referee Michael Oliver had no interest in appeals for a penalty when Tarik Muharemovic challenged Emmanuel Emegha inside the box.

Sources indicate that leeds handled Chelsea’s ventures forward well, mostly limiting the Blues to speculative efforts. Josh Acheamping, Morgan Rogers and Estevao all pulled the trigger from distance, yet little was asked of James Trafford between the Leeds sticks.

In a recent development, at the other end, Leeds continued to make inroads on the right. James Justin whipped a cross over for Calvert-Lewin, who struggled to generate power but did hit the crossbar with his looped header.

Industry observers note that leeds’ focus soon shifted to the left, where Gudmundsson started to flex his attacking muscles. He made an incisive dart into the box and went to ground under close attention from Estevao, although the referee paid no attention to penalty appeals.

Leeds’ left wing-back then picked out Calvert-Lewin and saw the England international force a strong hand from Emiliano Martinez with a headed effort.

Industry observers note that the visitors looked to be moving through the gears but just as the tide was turning, Chelsea drew first blood. Justin and Nico Elvedi both failed to stop the advancement of Rogers, who fed Emegha and saw the frontman beat Trafford at his near post with a blasted finish.

Leeds bit back almost immediately, levelling proceedings within three minutes of the opener. Calvert-Lewin contested a long ball with Wesley Fofana before picking up the scraps and releasing Okafor, who jinked his way into space and rifled across Martinez.

It has been revealed that with the wind behind their sails, Leeds came close to overturning the deficit via their equaliser’s creator. Calvert-Lewin met a Muharemovic cross and his deft flick came agonisingly close to finding the bottom corner.

Farke’s men continued applying pressure in the closing stages of the first half and Ao Tanaka was unfortunate to see a rasping rocket of a shot deflected before it could cause Martinez any trouble.

Gudmundsson then danced his way into an opportunity before poking harmlessly wide of Martinez’s right-hand post.

The next chance fell to Tanaka, who pushed the ball out of his feet but could only force a straightforward save with a shot straight down Martinez’s throat.

Leeds did have the ball in the back of the net on the stroke of half-time, although Justin was clearly offside before he delivered for Muharemovic to finish. When the half-time whistle did blow, it was Leeds firmly in the driving seat.

The second half started as the first ended, with Leeds in the ascendency. There were early appeals for a penalty when Calvert-Lewin tangled with Martinez, but Oliver was again dismissive of protests.

Tanaka then stretched to get on the end of a cross from deep, steering just off target as pressure piled on Chelsea.

Recent findings suggest that having seen their protests ignored mere minutes earlier, Leeds saw Oliver point to the spot when Rogers was judged to have handled a Muharemovic shot. After a lengthy VAR check, the decision was stuck by and Calvert-Lewin buried the spot-kick.

Chelsea responded by putting their front foot forward and Rogers forced Trafford down to his left with a low drive from distance.

However, it was Leeds who struck next and sent the the travelling supporters into a frenzy. After Chelsea failed to clear their lines after a long throw, Ethan Ampadu’s deflected cross was hammered home by Okafor in emphatic fashion.

Sources indicate that somewhat predictably, Chelsea surged back into the driving seat as they looked for a way back into a game getting away from them. Much to the frustration of the home supporters, their spell of control yielded little more than occasional half-chances.

There were sharp inhales of breath when Rogers arrowed a free-kick goalwards from a tight angle, but it dipped over the crossbar with Trafford at full stretch.

Many of Chelsea’s supporters were already heading out to beat the traffic when Aaronson capped an astonishing afternoon, wriggling through a creaking defence before steering a fourth past Martinez.
